title: 5 Years After the Fall: Why the World Still Misreads the Taliban
gist: Five years after the Taliban retook power in Afghanistan, the international community has cycled through humanitarian aid, political and economic pressure, and diplomatic engagement that has evolved from indirect to some direct talks, while Afghan civil society has sustained parallel resistance through underground schools, protests and civil disobedience.

themes.theme: International engagement strategies toward the Taliban

insights.claim: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan five years ago, the international community has tried a range of policies to influence its behavior, spanning humanitarian assistance, political and economic pressure, and diplomatic engagement that began through indirect channels and has, in some cases, developed into direct talks.
insights.speaker: Munera Yousufzada
insights.so_what: The shift from indirect to some direct talks with the Taliban signals a gradual, incremental path toward normalized channels with Kabul that observers of Afghanistan-related sanctions, aid flows and diplomacy should track.

insights.speaker: Munera Yousufzada
insights.so_what: Ongoing grassroots resistance, including underground schooling networks, indicates the Taliban has not achieved full social consolidation despite five years in power, relevant to any assessment of regime stability.

insights.speaker: Munera Yousufzada
insights.so_what: Continued anti-normalization efforts by civil society could complicate any move by foreign governments toward fuller diplomatic recognition of the Taliban.
